subject: knitted HTML table loses formatting in pandoc

messages.author: d567d0ef3c054a35
messages.subject: knitted HTML table loses formatting in pandoc
parts:
Greetings. I'm having a problem making slidify slides from an HTML file
produced by knitr: a section of the file that's supposed to be a table loses
its tabular structure after passing through pandoc.

I've appended the details.

This may be an issue with pandoc, or, more likely, my lack of understanding of
it, but maybe someone on this list has enough experience with both products to point
me in the right direction.

Thanks.

-- Mike


Software details
================

R version 3.0.1 (2013-05-16) -- "Good Sport"
Copyright (C) 2013 The R Foundation for Statistical Computing
Platform: x86_64-redhat-linux-gnu (64-bit)

knitr
Version: 1.2
Date: 2013-04-10

pandoc 1.9.4.5


Here's the command I use to produce the slide document:
======================================================

$ pandoc -s -S -i -t slidy --mathjax 01-what-is-probability.md -o
01-what-is-probability-slides.html

Here's the relevant piece of the Rmd file:
=========================================

### 5. Two dice example
--------------------------------
Roll a red die and a blue die and record (red die outcome, blue die outcome).
The sample space $S$ consists of the ordered pairs:

| | | | |
------- | ------- | ------- | ------- | ------- | -------
(1,1) | (1,2) | (1,3) | (1,4) | (1,5) | (1,6)

(6,1) | (6,2) | (6,3) | (6,4) | (6,5) | (6,6)


Here's the HTML code generated by knitting to HTML:

<p>Roll a red die and a blue die and record (red die outcome, blue die
outcome). The sample space \( S \) consists of the ordered pairs:</p>

outcome). The sample space \(S\) consists of the ordered pairs:</p>

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] knitted HTML table loses formatting in pandoc
parts:
Pandoc's table syntax is different with RStudio's (the so-called R
Markdown): http://johnmacfarlane.net/pandoc/README.html#tables

Markdown tables are painful. Everybody implements tables in different ways.

Regards,
Yihui
--

messages.author: d567d0ef3c054a35
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] knitted HTML table loses formatting in pandoc
parts:
Thanks, Yihui.  I've been reading through the pandoc documentation and had come to more or less the same conclusion: you can't get there from here.

The workaround that I'm using is to prefix each line of the table with four spaces.  knitr deals gracefully with that, and pandoc treats it as a literal block.  The resulting slide does contain the "scaffolding" for the table, but the table otherwise looks fine (and I don't find the scaffolding to be particularly offensive in any case).

-- Mike

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] knitted HTML table loses formatting in pandoc
parts:
In the devel version of knitr (https://github.com/yihui/knitr) I have
a kable() function, which recognizes the output format when it is
called inside knitr. For your case, you can set
options(knitr.table.format = 'pandoc') (or 'markdown') so that the
appropriate table format can be used.

Regards,
Yihui
--

messages.author: 8c8f0ca54c4a2459
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] knitted HTML table loses formatting in pandoc
parts:
Pandoc now accepts a variety of table formats if you specify them. Try

pandoc -s -S -i -f markdown+pipe_tables -t slidy --mathjax 01-what-is-probability.md -o 01-what-is-probability-slides.html

On Thursday, July 11, 2013 3:12:00 PM UTC-7, Yihui Xie wrote:
In the devel version of knitr (https://github.com/yihui/knitr) I have
a kable() function, which recognizes the output format when it is
called inside knitr. For your case, you can set
options(knitr.table.format = 'pandoc') (or 'markdown') so that the
appropriate table format can be used.

Regards,
Yihui
